title: SSi register codex: is a pod turn part of a SERVICE encounter?
purpose: extract-dialogue-patterns.cjs reports which registers attest each dialogue frame. Sector (clinical) rows are clinical by source; every other pod turn is service or social, judged here by a Haiku-family model instead of a regex over speaker and scene names (r-2026-10-07-never-use-regex-to-classify-language).
task: You decide whether a turn from a language-course dialogue belongs to a service encounter
request: For EACH numbered item (speaker | scene | turn), give R1 if the turn is part of a service encounter, or - if it is social. Never output O.
example: Example: 3: speaker is a barista serving coffee => R1
general_rules: A SERVICE encounter is one where one person serves the other in a commercial or professional role: buying, ordering, paying, booking, checking in, asking a shop assistant, a pharmacist, a receptionist, a driver, a ticket clerk, a bank clerk, or asking a passer-by (a local) for directions.

The SPEAKER is the strongest signal: a role name (Barista, Waiter, Receptionist, Driver, Shopkeeper, Pharmacist, Clerk, Cashier, Staff, Local, Customer, Passenger, Guest) means a service encounter, and so does a personal name when the turn is plainly the customer side of one.
The SCENE title helps but can mislead: a counter transaction can sit inside a scene titled as greetings. Judge the turn in its scene, not the title alone.
Friends, family, colleagues or strangers chatting, greeting, catching up or making plans are SOCIAL (-).
output: One line per item: '<number>: <a few words> => R1' or '=> -'.

frames.name: service encounter
frames.shape: speaker in a serving role, or a customer addressing one
frames.definition: The turn belongs to a service encounter: someone serving (selling, taking an order, checking in, giving directions as a local) or the customer side of that exchange.
positives: Barista | A Day of Greetings (iii) - 3 pm | Here's your coffee.
Waiter | At the restaurant | Are you ready to order?
Tom | At the chemist | Have you got anything for a headache?
Receptionist | Checking in | Your room is on the second floor.
Local | Asking for directions | It's the second street on the left.

near_misses.text: Aran | A Day of Greetings (i) | Good morning, how are you?
Mum | At home | Do you want a coffee?
Sara | Meeting a friend at the coffee shop | It's so good to see you!
near_misses.why: friends chatting in a café: the setting is commercial, the encounter is social

near_misses.text: Colleague | At work | Shall we have lunch?
Tom | Planning the weekend | We could go to the market.
near_misses.why: talking ABOUT a shop is not a service encounter

boundary: The encounter type decides, not the place: friends in a café are social; a customer at the counter is service.
